name: Canberra Times cryptic crossword, Sunday 5 February 1984

clue.text: Procure without right could make compensation

indicators.note: 'without' means lacking, so one letter is taken away from the word before it
'could make' suggests what the remaining letters might become if rearranged into another word

blocks.note: taken as written
R is the standard abbreviation for right; one of the two Rs is dropped

explanation.surface: Obtaining something without having any right to it might oblige you to pay damages.
explanation.walkthrough: Drop one R from PROCURE and the six letters left rearrange into RECOUP.
explanation.definitionFit: To recoup is to make good a loss, reimbursing or compensating oneself or another.

clue.text: Some of the beer I enjoyed was rather weird

indicators.note: 'some of' means only a part of the following words is wanted, a run of consecutive letters

blocks.note: the run starts inside the second word and ends at the start of the last

explanation.surface: The beer someone drank had a strange taste.
explanation.definitionFit: Eerie means strange in an unsettling, uncanny way, so it fits being somewhat weird.

clue.text: A third-rate actor with nothing comes up to Ne braska

definitions.note: the answer is a city in Nebraska, not the state itself

indicators.note: in a down entry 'comes up' means the letters read from the bottom upwards, so they are written backwards

blocks.note: taken as written
a ham is a bad, overacting performer
O looks like a zero

explanation.surface: A poor actor with no prospects makes his way to the Midwest.
explanation.walkthrough: A + HAM + O, written upwards, gives OMAHA. The newspaper text splits 'Nebraska'; the definition points to a place in that state rather than the state itself.
explanation.definitionFit: Omaha is the largest city in the US state of Nebraska, on the Missouri River.

clue.text: A.I. report for characters in South African city

indicators.note: 'characters in' says use only the letters of what came before, in a new order

blocks.note: taken as written, ignoring the full stops

explanation.surface: An Amnesty International report on people in a South African city.
explanation.walkthrough: In 1984 A.I. would most readily read as Amnesty International, whose reports on South Africa were in the news.
explanation.definitionFit: Pretoria is South Africa's administrative capital, in Gauteng province.

clue.text: Star components of Peter or Ivan

indicators.note: 'components of' says the parts of the word are taken apart and put together again differently

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Peter or Ivan is the name of a celestial body's component.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Peter or Ivan' sounds like two ordinary men's names; they are Peter the Great and Ivan the Terrible.
explanation.definitionFit: Peter the Great and Ivan the Terrible were both rulers of Russia, each an example of its emperor.

clue.text: Extractor of knowledge initially earns dollars under certain easy rules

indicators.note: 'initially' asks for the opening letter of each word that follows

blocks.clueFragment: earns dollars under certain easy rules
blocks.note: the first letter of each of the six words

explanation.surface: Someone who draws out knowledge makes money under lenient regulations.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Initially' seems to modify 'earns' alone, but it governs every word after it.
explanation.definitionFit: To educe is to draw out or elicit, so an educer is one who brings out latent facts or ideas.

clue.text: It's mad to be stupid round the pole

indicators.note: 'round' says one piece goes around another, enclosing it

blocks.note: inane means silly or senseless
S, for the South Pole, is a common crossword pole

explanation.surface: It's crazy to behave foolishly near the Pole.
explanation.definitionFit: Insane and mad are synonyms, both describing someone out of their mind.

clue.text: Inhabitant gets rent round the lateral part

indicators.note: 'round' says one word wraps around the other, enclosing it in the middle

blocks.note: taken as written; it is split after its second letter
the lateral part of anything is its side

explanation.surface: A tenant pays rent for a flat in the side wing of a building.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rent' reads as the payment a dweller makes, but it is just the outer word, split after its second letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A resident is a person who lives in a place, the same as an inhabitant of it.

clue.text: A tenor, elaborately deco rated, in a way

indicators.note: 'elaborately' suggests intricate reworking, so the letters before it are rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A tenor singer turns up in elaborate, decorated costume.
explanation.walkthrough: The newspaper text splits 'decorated' as 'deco rated'. 'Elaborately' looks as if it belongs with the definition, but it is the rearranging signal, leaving 'decorated, in a way'.
explanation.definitionFit: Something ornate is heavily ornamented, which is one particular way of being decorated.

clue.text: Not a curt kind of deserter

indicators.note: 'kind of' says the letters before it form only a version of something, so they are rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A polite defector who is never short with anyone.
explanation.definitionFit: A turncoat abandons their party or cause for the other side, a betrayer who deserts.

clue.text: Gale to upset smooth musical direction

indicators.note: 'upset' means knocked over and thrown into disorder, so the letters are jumbled

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A storm disturbs the calm, flowing playing an orchestra was asked for.
explanation.definitionFit: Legato is the Italian term written in a score telling players to join the notes smoothly.

clue.text: It's always being changed these days

definitions.text: It's always being changed these days

blocks.clueFragment: It's always being changed these days
blocks.note: surface reading: something under constant revision in modern life, like fashions or rules
setter's reading: the part of a car the driver keeps shifting, and also clothes, which are changed every day

explanation.walkthrough: Drivers are forever changing gear, and gear is also slang for clothes, which people change daily.
explanation.definitionFit: A car's gear is constantly changed while driving, and gear also means clothing or kit.

clue.text: Give ear to Peter making kind of snappy reply

indicators.note: 'making' says the joined letters are worked into something new, so they are rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Listen to Peter and you will hear his quick-witted comebacks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Give ear to' reads as the idiom for listening, but here it only joins the two words before their letters are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Repartee is quick, witty conversational retort, a sort of sharp comeback.

clue.text: Stripe, e.g., might result in high standing

indicators.note: 'might result in' says the letters before it could be reworked to produce something else

blocks.note: taken as written, including the abbreviation e.g.

explanation.surface: A stripe on a uniform, such as a sergeant's, could earn one a high rank.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'e.g.' looks like it introduces an example, but its two letters are part of the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Prestige is widespread respect and esteem, a high reputation or status.

clue.text: Return portion of the snare

indicators.note: 'return' means turn back, so the next word is read from end to start

blocks.note: a portion is a part

explanation.surface: Give back a share of the drum kit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Portion of' looks like the signal for a run of letters hidden in 'the snare', but nothing is hidden there.
explanation.definitionFit: A trap and a snare are both devices for catching animals.

clue.text: Get sailor, or return to entrance and repeal the law

indicators.note: 'return' means go back, so the short word before it is written backwards

blocks.note: AB, able-bodied seaman, is the usual crossword sailor
taken as written
a gate is an entrance

explanation.surface: Fetch a seaman or head back to the door, then overturn the regulations.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Or' looks like a conjunction offering a choice, but it is two letters to be turned round.
explanation.definitionFit: To abrogate is formally to abolish or annul a law or agreement.

clue.text: Increases the power of Puss-end in boots

indicators.note: 'end' attached to the word asks for only its final letter
'in' says one piece sits inside the next one

blocks.note: taken as written; it opens after its fourth letter
the last letter of this word

explanation.surface: The fairy-tale cat Puss in Boots gains strength by the end.
explanation.walkthrough: The last letter of Puss goes into BOOTS: BOO-S-TS.
explanation.definitionFit: To boost is to raise or amplify, so boosts means makes more powerful.

clue.text: Musical shows for some of those who elope rashly

indicators.note: 'some of' says only a stretch of the following words is wanted

blocks.note: the run starts in the middle of 'elope' and ends three letters into the last word

explanation.surface: Musical entertainments are made for couples who run off to marry on impulse.
explanation.definitionFit: Operas are dramas set to music and sung, a type of staged musical performance.

clue.text: U.S. uncle with woodland Deity in Chinese boat

blocks.note: Uncle Sam personifies the United States
Pan is the Greek god of woods, shepherds and flocks

explanation.surface: An American uncle and a forest god go aboard a vessel in China.
explanation.definitionFit: A sampan is a small flat-bottomed skiff used on rivers and coasts in China and East Asia.

clue.text: Low to the south-east it's large with antlers

definitions.note: a description of the animal rather than a noun

blocks.note: to low is to make the sound of cattle
SE is the compass abbreviation

explanation.surface: A beast lowing off to the south-east is a big creature with horns.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Low' reads as an adjective, the opposite of high, but it is the verb for the cattle sound.
explanation.definitionFit: The moose is the largest deer, the male bearing broad, flattened antlers.

clue.text: At getting round U.S. troops to feed cattle

indicators.note: 'getting round' says the first piece goes around the next, enclosing it

blocks.note: taken as written; it opens after its first letter
GIs are American soldiers

explanation.surface: American soldiers are rounded up to give food to a herd.
explanation.walkthrough: Agist is a farming and legal term, common in Australia, for taking in other people's stock to graze for a fee.
explanation.definitionFit: To agist is to take livestock onto one's land to graze, usually for payment, so it means pasturing them.

clue.text: Lave toes erratically in amorous chair

indicators.note: 'erratically' means without regular order, so the letters are scrambled

blocks.note: taken as written; lave is an old word for wash

explanation.surface: Someone washes their feet clumsily while sitting in a romantic seat.
explanation.definitionFit: A loveseat is a small sofa for two people, so it is a chair suited to sweethearts.

clue.text: Give out part of a semitone

indicators.note: 'part of' says the answer is a piece of the words that follow

blocks.note: the run sits just inside the second word

explanation.surface: Sing out part of a half-step in music.
explanation.definitionFit: To emit is to send forth or discharge sound, light or gas, the same as giving it out.

clue.text: Press 99 to be perversely fitting

blocks.note: to iron clothes is to press them
in loose Roman numerals I before C is one less than a hundred

explanation.surface: Pressing 99 on a keypad turns out oddly appropriate.
explanation.walkthrough: Strict Roman numerals write 99 as XCIX; the setter uses the informal subtractive form IC.
explanation.definitionFit: An ironic outcome is apt in a contrary way, fitting precisely because it upsets what was expected.

clue.text: Wandering off to upset sting ray

indicators.note: 'upset' means overturned and disordered, so the letters after it are jumbled

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A diver drifts away so as not to disturb a stingray.
explanation.definitionFit: Straying means drifting from the proper path or place, the same as wandering away.

clue.text: Chooses the Spanish kind of sect

indicators.note: 'kind of' says the next word appears only in some version, so its letters are rearranged

blocks.note: el is Spanish for 'the'
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone picks out a particular type of Spanish religious group.
explanation.definitionFit: To elect is to pick, most often by vote, so elects is a synonym of chooses.
